thisFork.rationale: Adversarial-review fixes for the critical and high findings shared between two independent reviews (notebook-library URL poisoning, sessionStorage origin-pin bypass, single-file upload denylist gap, read-only-token-can-mutate, chat-history arbitrary file write). Marketing claims trimmed to honest scope. Supply-chain CI gates added (exact-pin enforcement, Sigstore signature verification, lockfile-drift detection, npm audit ratchet).

securityHardening._doc: Concrete code-level controls. Verify each against SECURITY.md and the test suite — these are claims, not certifications.
securityHardening.auditLogging: hash-chained, cross-day linkage, tamper-detect on read
securityHardening.mcpAuthentication: SHA3-256 + persistent salt; constant-time compare; admin/read scopes
securityHardening.secureByDefaultAuth: auth on by default; explicit NLMCP_AUTH_DISABLED=true to opt out
securityHardening.responseValidation: pattern-based prompt-injection + URL detector (defence-in-depth, not a silver bullet)
securityHardening.localAtRestEncryption: ChaCha20-Poly1305 + ML-KEM-768 hybrid; both keys live on the same host (offline-disk-theft scope only)
securityHardening.memoryScrubbing: Buffer-level zero-fill; JS strings remain in V8 heap until GC
securityHardening.webhookSsrfProtection: scheme + lexical-IP + DNS-resolution + send-time revalidation; redirects refused
securityHardening.supplyChainGates: exact-version pins + Sigstore signature verification + lockfile-drift check + npm audit ratchet in CI

complianceControls._doc: Code-level primitives. Compliance is an organisational property — these features are necessary, not sufficient. Formal certification requires a third-party audit covering policies, training, vendor management, and incident response procedures.

gdpr.rightToErasure: best-effort logical wipe; cannot guarantee on SSD/CoW filesystems without full-disk encryption

soc2.incidentResponse: incident manager primitives — does not replace IR plan
